shippingNews.postTitle: USCG Buoy Tender Sequoia Towed Back to Port Huron

stories.body: USCG Sequoia under tow of Erica Kobasic and Nickelena. [Rosann Hollinger] STURGEON BAY, WI – The USCG buoy tender Sequoia has been at Bay Shipbuilding Co. in Sturgeon Bay, WI, for gearbox repairs the past several months, but Monday she was headed back to her Port Huron, MI, home port under tow. The tug Nickelena was on the bow and Erika Kobasic was at the stern. A new gearbox is being made and Sequoia will return to the yard in the spring to have it installed. shippingNews.postTitle: Gaelic Tugboat Launches Tralee at Detroit

stories.body: DETROIT, MI – On Monday, Oct. 19, Gaelic Tugboat Co.’s newest acquisition, the tug Tralee, formerly the Lauren A., was launched at the company’s dock on the Rouge River in Detroit. Tralee was previously owned by White Lake Dock and Dredge in West Michigan. Tralee replaces the tug Patricia Hoey, which made her final run on October 13. In keeping with the company’s Irish heritage, the tug is named after Tralee, a town on the northern side of the neck of the Dingle Peninsula in Ireland, and is the largest town in County Kerry. todayInHistory.title: Sam Laud
todayInHistory.text: Sam Laud Bay Shipbuilding Corp. of Sturgeon Bay, WI, laid the keel for their hull # 712 on Jan. 4, 1974 to be built as a smaller-sized Great Lakes self-unloading bulk cargo carrier. The new vessel was launched on Nov. 19, 1974 for Buffalo's American Steamship Co. (ASC), a subsidiary of GATX Corp., Chicago, IL. Completed in 1975, the self-unloader was christened Sam Laud by Mrs. Edna Laud on behalf of her husband at a christening ceremony held April 15, 1975. Mr. Laud was the former president (1945) and chairman of the board (1956) of GATX Corp., having started with the company in 1916 as shop painter and riveter. Mr. Laud died August 1, 1963. GATX Corp. had acquired ASC in July of 1973. Mrs. Laud was accompanied by Mr. Frederick G. Jaicks, chairman and CEO of Inland Steel Co., Chicago, IL, who gave the address at the christening ceremonies. One of a new generation of self-unloaders for the ASC fleet, the Sam Laud was built at an approximate cost of $13.3 million and was the fourth of 10 self-unloaders launched for the fleet under Chapter XI of the Merchant Marine Act of 1970. Under this act, the U.S. government-guaranteed financing and tax deferred benefits for fleet modernizing. The other ASC self-unloaders built under this program were the Roger M. Kyes (now Adam E. Cornelius, 1973), Charles E. Wilson (now John J. Boland, 1973), H. Lee White (1974), St. Clair (1976), Belle River (now Walter J. marineWeather.synopsis: A 30.4 inch high pressure over Quebec extending 30.1 inch ridging westwards over Lake Superior weakens to 30.2 inches today over New England and the Lower Great Lakes. Meanwhile, a weak 30.0 inch trough moves over the lake. Another high pressure builds in from the west in its wake, becoming centered over northern Ontario and the Upper Great Lakes by Thursday morning. By Friday afternoon, the high builds to 30.5 inches over the Ontario/Quebec line as a 29.4 inch low moves into eastern Montana. Saturday afternoon, the high builds further to 30.6 inches over New England as the 29.4 inch low moves just north of Lake Winnipeg. The low then lifts northeast to Hudson Bay on Sunday dragging a 30.2 inch trough across the lake.

A ridge of 30.3 inch high pressure is centered from the Mississippi River into Ontario this morning, resulting in light south to southwest winds across the open waters. Winds will trend light and variable tonight through Thursday night as the surface ridge nudges east toward the Ohio River and Quebec. Persistent southerly winds will become established Friday through the weekend as a cold front moves through the northern Great Plains and 30.5 inch high pressure settles into the northeastern United States. Winds could be breezy at times, with widespread gales not anticipated at this time. Will continue to monitor for possible increases through the second half of the week. Aforementioned cold front will cross the waters Sunday night, bringing a northerly wind shift through the first half of next week. Rain showers are possible along the passing front.
A weak and dry cold front will track through the central Great Lakes tonight. Another large high pressure, 30.40 inches, then builds over the area Thursday and Friday.

High pressure will maintain influence over Lake Erie for the next several days. The high will weaken to 30.20 inches today and Thursday, before re-intensfying to 30.40 inches over southern Ontario Thursday night into Friday.

A high pressure ridge averaging 30.4 inches exits slowly toward the Canadian Maritimes before a weak cold front sweeps southeastward across the lake on Thursday. Behind the front, another ridge averaging 30.5 inches affects the lake through this weekend as the embedded high pressure center moves southeastward across the Great Lakes through Friday and then moves farther southeastward to Atlantic waters near Long Island and New Jersey by this Sunday.
